clue.text: Ambassador, unfortunately born somewhere in the Middle East

parts.note: an ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately go wrong, so the letters of born are set awry

explanation.surface: A diplomat laments being born in some Middle Eastern posting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebron is a city in the West Bank, a place in the Middle East.

clue.text: How to save energy? Party 'n' dance!

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so the word how holds the next letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
a do is a party
the shortened and stands for the letter N

explanation.surface: A tip for cutting power use, then a party and a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a question then a slogan; in fact 'to save' puts E plus DO inside HOW, with the N of 'n' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance, or a gathering for such dancing.

clue.text: Bishop down under said to have sex with animal

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: in Australian slang, which is what down under signals, root is a coarse word for sex
said tells us the word is spoken, so we keep its sound and respell it

parts.note: root is Australian slang for having sex

explanation.surface: A scandalous tale of an Australian clergyman and a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' points to Australia, where ROOT means to have sex; 'said' gives its sound, spelt RUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a beast, a non-human creature.

clue.text: Poor soul struggling with ICT, an old medic

indicators.note: struggling suggests thrashing about, so the letters are jumbled together with ICT
poor here means in a sorry state, so the letters of soul are disordered first

explanation.surface: A sad figure battling with information technology lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' signals the anagram of SOUL plus ICT (Information and Communication Technology, a British school subject); 'Poor' already muddles SOUL, which changes nothing in the final shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Oculist is a dated word for an eye doctor, hence an old-fashioned medic.

clue.text: Chemical weapon in the end located next to a tree

indicators.note: the end of the word in is its final letter

parts.note: a palm is a kind of tree

explanation.surface: A chemical weapon is finally found hidden beside a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is an incendiary jelly used in bombs, a chemical weapon.

clue.text: Ultimately, it may show you where China is: north of Thailand

parts.words: it may show you where China is
parts.note: a book of maps would show where China lies

indicators.note: in a down entry, the north of a word is its top, the first letter

explanation.surface: A geography lesson: China lies north of Thailand.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'north of' means the topmost letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: At last means finally, in the end, as ultimately does.

clue.text: American 'King of Swing' unknown to quite a few

parts.note: Benny Goodman, clarinettist and bandleader, was nicknamed the King of Swing
y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An American jazz great was unknown to plenty of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A good many is an idiom for a considerable number.

clue.text: Cameron's wrong, missing a point — he's noted for being controversial

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are set out incorrectly, so they are rearranged
missing tells us the letter a is lost from the name

parts.note: taken as written, the former Prime Minister's surname
E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Former PM David Cameron is in the wrong over a pointless controversy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes A from CAMERON, leaving CMERON; add E and 'wrong' shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: John McEnroe, the tennis champion, was famous for disputing umpires' calls.

clue.text: A-Ha in concert, surprisingly, including one Diana Ross song

indicators.note: including means the jumbled letters take one inside them
surprisingly hints the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Norwegian band A-Ha unexpectedly cover a Diana Ross number live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges AHAINCONCERT, and 'including' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain Reaction was a 1986 hit single for Diana Ross, written by the Bee Gees.

clue.text: List of prime numbers

indicators.note: of here means drawn out of, so the letters are taken from inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A mathematician's catalogue of primes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime numbers' looks like maths; the answer sits across the join of the two words, after 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is a list, whether of dishes in a restaurant or options on a screen.

clue.text: Group of nations gave permission to describe Hungary as profane

indicators.note: to describe in the geometric sense is to draw a line round, so the letters enclose another

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, is a group of nations
allowed means gave permission
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: The UN allowed members to call Hungary ungodly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line round something; H is the vehicle code for Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhallowed means not consecrated, unholy, so profane is a synonym.

clue.text: Song by Dutch rock band featured in Love Island

indicators.note: featured in means placed within the letters from love and island

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
REM is the American rock band

explanation.surface: A Dutch rock group's song appears on the reality show Love Island.
explanation.walkthrough: Love Island is a British TV dating show; here it splits into O and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Do-Re-Mi is the song from The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Prisoners perhaps people with specific knowledge?

definitions.meaning: people who are locked up are, jokingly, those on the inside
those within an organisation who know its secrets

explanation.definitionFit: Insiders are people within a group who hold privileged information; prisoners are also literally inside.

clue.text: Oddly, some seen around rocky peak after today's bad weather

indicators.note: seen around means these two letters are found surrounding what follows
oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word some
after puts the peak behind what comes next in the clue

parts.note: today is now, plus the possessive s
a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Odd sightings near a craggy summit following the day's foul weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' and 'seen around' work on 'some' alone, its odd letters wrapping everything after; 'today's' keeps its S. A tor is a rocky hill in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowstorm is a heavy fall of snow with wind, a kind of bad weather.

clue.text: Mineral water at first welcome, liquid low in calories

indicators.note: at first means take only the opening letter of water

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome
l is the chemistry state symbol for liquid
lite is a label for food or drink with fewer calories

explanation.surface: Mineral water greets you, a liquid lite on calories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mineral water' looks like one phrase, but Mineral alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wavellite is a phosphate mineral of aluminium, found in radiating crystals.

clue.text: For classicists, sea horse

definitions.meaning: in Latin, the language of classicists, the word for sea

explanation.definitionFit: Mare is Latin for sea and English for an adult female horse.

clue.text: Jealousy when diplomat says goodbye to Ohio

indicators.note: saying goodbye to something means letting it leave, so a letter departs

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic messenger
O is a standard abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: Resentment stirs as a diplomat leaves the state of Ohio.
explanation.definitionFit: Envy is a covetous resentment of others, close in sense to jealousy.

clue.text: "Me? In real trouble?" (D. Green)

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of me and real are churned up

explanation.surface: A worried speaker asks if they are in real trouble, signed by D. Green.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a signature, but D is a letter and Green the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright shade of green, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Within three years, Kate developed a knack — finally! — for stupid talk

indicators.note: within means the shuffled name sits inside the three letters

parts.note: y is an abbreviation for year, so three of them

indicators.note: developed means changed in form, so the name's letters are rearranged
finally means take the last letter of knack

explanation.surface: Kate, after three years, finally learns the art of idle chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges KATE to AKET, which 'Within' places among the three Ys, after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakety-yak is informal for incessant trivial chatter, idle prattle.

clue.text: Introduction of Cavani in added time should make you concentrate

indicators.note: in places the initial within the following letters

parts.note: extra means added

indicators.note: the introduction of a name is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Bringing on striker Edinson Cavani in stoppage time should focus the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentrate' is a noun here: an extract is a concentrated essence.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a concentrated preparation drawn from a substance, a concentrate.

clue.text: Get rid of Member of Congress, leaving shambolic mess

indicators.note: a mess is disorder, so the letters left over are scrambled

parts.note: MC is the abbreviation for Member of Congress

explanation.surface: A call to remove a US lawmaker from a chaotic situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes MC out of SHAMBOLIC; 'mess' rearranges the remaining SHABOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to do away with something formally, to get rid of it.

clue.text: Car to avoid on motorway

parts.note: to dodge is to avoid
M designates a British motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A car you would do well to steer clear of on the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodgem is a bumper car at a fairground.

clue.text: Lake to be tricky for yacht

indicators.note: tricky suggests something awkward and twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lake proves difficult to sail for a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelboat is a sailing yacht with a fixed keel.

clue.text: People opposing us having died as criminals

parts.note: them is the other side in us and them
ob is short for obiit, Latin for died

explanation.surface: Our enemies died as gangsters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mob is a collective term for organised crime, the Mafia.

clue.text: Highly praise English tax reforms being blocked by Left

indicators.note: being blocked by means another letter gets in the way, sitting inside
reforms means reshapes, so the letters of tax are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praising English tax changes that are obstructed by the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' gives XAT from TAX, and 'being blocked by' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt is to extol or glorify, praising very highly.

clue.text: Graduate at Cambridge college having trouble all round finding possible antacid

parts.note: BA is Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
King's is a Cambridge college

indicators.note: all round means turned about, so the word for trouble runs backwards

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A Cambridge graduate with stomach trouble seeks an antacid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all round' turns ADO back to front, giving ODA; King's College keeps no apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking soda, sodium bicarbonate, neutralises stomach acid, so it can serve as an antacid.

clue.text: Greedy king beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the head, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: David was a biblical king of Israel

explanation.surface: A grasping monarch meets a grisly end.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means eager or keen, here in the sense of greedy for something.

clue.text: Tesla quits inner part of Amsterdam: misplaced ambitions

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong position, so the remaining letters are rearranged
quits means leaves, so a letter goes from those inner letters
the inner part of a word is all but its outer letters

parts.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: Tesla abandons central Amsterdam, its ambitions misguided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inner part of' gives MSTERDA; 'quits' removes T (the tesla, not the carmaker) to leave MSERDA, and 'misplaced' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreams are aspirations or hopes, so ambitions is a synonym.

clue.text: Pain caused by former Wimbledon champion grabbing first of titles

indicators.note: grabbing means the name holds a letter inside it

parts.note: Michael Stich won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1991

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of titles

explanation.surface: An ex-champion's pain at snatching the first of his titles.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain in the side, as when running.
